_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the POS Sync roadmap rendered at /extensions/pos-sync/roadmap. Task `status` is maintained AUTOMATICALLY by `node scripts/gen-pos-roadmap.mjs`, which inspects the real extension source tree and flips a task to `done` when everything in its `detect` block exists. Hand-edit title/detail/detect freely; set `pin: true` on a task whose status the script should leave alone.

milestones.title: Foundation — the ledger
milestones.goal: A provider-agnostic core that can record, queue and replay commerce events safely. Nothing here talks to a POS or to a cart; it is the neutral middle that makes the whole system N+M instead of N×M.

tasks.title: Extension scaffold
tasks.detail: `manifest.php`, the extension class, and a Settings screen under Unyson+ → POS Sync. Ships inactive by default, like the Animation Engine.

tasks.title: Ledger schema + migrations
tasks.detail: Three custom tables — `pos_items` (canonical item + external ids), `pos_events` (immutable sale / refund / stock-movement log), `pos_map` (external id ↔ local id, per connection). Versioned migrations run on activation and upgrade.

tasks.title: Idempotency ledger
tasks.detail: Every inbound event carries an external transaction id, stored behind a UNIQUE index. A replayed webhook is recorded as a duplicate and dropped — never applied twice. This is the single most important correctness guarantee in the extension.

tasks.title: Job queue on Action Scheduler
tasks.detail: Inbound events are acknowledged fast and applied asynchronously with retry + exponential backoff, so a slow cart write never times out a POS webhook. Uses Action Scheduler when present (every WooCommerce install has it), with a WP-Cron fallback.

tasks.title: Audit log + viewer
tasks.detail: A readable, filterable record of every event: what arrived, what was applied, what was skipped and why. The first thing anyone opens when a stock number looks wrong.

milestones.title: Store driver seam
milestones.goal: One interface between the ledger and whatever e-commerce plugin is installed — designed against two implementations from day one so it cannot leak WooCommerce assumptions.

tasks.title: `FW_POS_Store` interface
tasks.detail: The abstract contract: `find_by_sku()`, `set_stock()`, `adjust_stock()`, `create_order()`, `refund_order()`, `get_capabilities()`. Deliberately written while sketching both the Woo and FluentCart implementations.

tasks.title: WooCommerce store driver
tasks.detail: The shipping implementation — stock writes through `wc_update_product_stock()`, order creation with the POS sale recorded as the payment method, refund restocking, variation-aware SKU lookup.

tasks.title: SKU / GTIN matcher + unmatched queue
tasks.detail: Matching is by **SKU first, GTIN second, never by title**. Items that match nothing land in an *Unmatched* queue for one-click mapping or product creation, instead of silently vanishing.

tasks.title: Capability negotiation
tasks.detail: Carts differ — not all support partial refunds or per-location stock. Drivers declare what they can do, and the ledger degrades gracefully instead of throwing.

milestones.title: Generic webhook API
milestones.goal: The headline feature. A documented, signed, normalized endpoint any POS — or any middleware, or a shop's own till software — can push to. No vendor SDK, nothing to break when someone else's API changes.

tasks.title: REST namespace `unysonplus-pos/v1`
tasks.detail: `POST /sale`, `POST /refund`, `POST /inventory`, `GET /ping`. Fast acknowledgement (`202 Accepted`) with the event handed to the queue.

tasks.title: HMAC-SHA256 signing + replay window
tasks.detail: Every request carries `X-UPOS-Signature` and `X-UPOS-Timestamp`. Signatures are compared with `hash_equals()`, timestamps outside a ±5-minute window are rejected, and seen nonces are cached for the window length.

tasks.title: Normalized payload schema v1
tasks.detail: A published, versioned JSON Schema for sale / refund / inventory payloads, validated on ingest so a malformed till can never corrupt the ledger.

tasks.title: Connections: keys, scopes, rotation
tasks.detail: Each till or integration is a named *connection* with its own key/secret pair, scopes, location mapping and last-seen timestamp. Rotate or revoke one without touching the others.

milestones.title: Virtual Terminal
milestones.goal: The answer to “I don't own a POS machine.” A shipping feature that fires realistic synthetic events at your own endpoint — the development test rig, the customer's pre-launch check, and the demo for these docs, all at once.

tasks.title: Virtual Terminal screen
tasks.detail: Pick products, quantities and a location; fire a signed sale, refund or stock adjustment and watch it land in the log and move real stock.

tasks.title: Adversarial scenario presets
tasks.detail: One click each for the cases that break naive integrations: **duplicate webhook**, **out-of-order offline batch**, **partial refund**, **unknown SKU**, **stock below zero**, **expired signature**. These double as the automated test suite.

tasks.title: Signed request / cURL export
tasks.detail: Copy a correctly-signed example request for any scenario, so an integrator can reproduce it from their own till software or Postman.

milestones.title: Square driver (first-party)
milestones.goal: One polished vendor driver, chosen for the best free sandbox and the largest small-retail footprint. Proves the provider seam without committing to five vendor APIs.

tasks.title: `FW_POS_Provider` interface
tasks.detail: The mirror of the store seam, on the POS side: connect, subscribe, normalize, backfill.

tasks.title: Square OAuth connect + token refresh
tasks.detail: Connect a Square account without pasting tokens; refresh before expiry and surface a clear re-connect prompt when a grant is revoked.

tasks.title: Webhook subscription + signature verification
tasks.detail: Subscribes to `payment.created`, `order.updated`, `refund.created` and `inventory.count.updated`, verifying Square's own signature before normalizing into the ledger.

tasks.title: Catalog import + mapping
tasks.detail: Pull the Square catalog, match to products by SKU, and present the unmatched remainder for mapping or creation.

tasks.title: Location → stock source mapping
tasks.detail: Map each Square location to a stock source, or run in explicit single-store mode. Never left implicit.

milestones.title: Reconciliation & operations
milestones.goal: The difference between a demo and something a shop can open the doors with. Assume events will be missed, and make drift visible and fixable.

tasks.title: Authority policy engine
tasks.detail: Per-field source of truth — the POS owns **stock**, the store owns **content** (title, description, images, SEO) — with a per-product override. Symmetric two-way sync with no declared authority is exactly what produces drift and oversells.

tasks.title: Nightly reconciliation sweep
tasks.detail: Compares POS counts against store stock, reports every divergence, and offers a one-click resync. Catches whatever the event stream dropped.

tasks.title: Timestamp-ordered application
tasks.detail: Offline tills dump batches late and out of order. Events are applied by **event timestamp, not arrival order**, so a late batch cannot rewind newer stock.

tasks.title: Health dashboard + alerts
tasks.detail: Queue depth, last event per connection, failure rate, and an email when a connection stalls or the queue backs up past a threshold.

milestones.title: Expansion (post-1.0)
milestones.goal: Only once the seams have proven themselves against real installs. Deliberately not launch scope.

tasks.title: FluentCart store driver
tasks.detail: The genuine second target — WP-native, custom tables, no first-party POS story of its own.

tasks.title: SureCart / EDD drivers
tasks.detail: Cheap to add once the seam has been proven by a second real implementation.

tasks.title: Clover / Zettle / Lightspeed drivers
tasks.detail: Added on demonstrated demand, in that order. Each is bespoke and maintenance-heavy — the generic webhook already covers them adequately.

tasks.title: Offline CSV / batch importer
tasks.detail: For tills with no network integration at all: a scheduled CSV drop reconciled through the same ledger.
